newsitem.title: USA: Perot running mate urges flexible US trade policy.
newsitem.headline: Perot running mate urges flexible US trade policy.

text.p: Ross Perot's Reform Party candidate for vice president, Pat Choate, said Monday that U.S. trade policy needed to be more flexible and recognize different economic structures around around the world.
"The United States is pursuing a very ethnocentric trade policy, one based on Anglo-American price theory principles," Choate said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"The United States harangues on other countries to be more like us -- a very arrogant policy -- when other countries don't wish to be like the United States," he said.

"The United States must be more tolerant, it must be more practical, it must be must less ideological, it must have trade policies that deal with countries as they are and not as we would wish them to be," he added.

He said, though, that the United States needs a trade policy that reflects the country's moral values. He said that in joining the World Trade Organization, the United States gave up the right to exclude from import products made by child labor.
Choate said he expects Perot to make trade a major campaign issue in his presidential campaign and that the subject will continue in the public debate after the November elections.
"After this campaign, trade will be as much of an issue as the budget was in 1993," he said.
